title: Meadow Rotations
rules: Gates change real passage between three fenced meadows. Toggle from Manhattan distance at most one.
Herds move on even ticks toward visible grass or, when thirsty, a trough. They take one greedy legal step, not a hidden planned route.
A plot rests only with no herd within one cell. After two rest ticks it regenerates one grass per tick, up to six.
Hunger rises every two ticks and thirst every three. A herd eats only on a grass cell and drinks only on a trough.
Healthy fed herds produce one milk on every fourth tick, up to three stored. Carry one milk to the shared barn.
Every herd entry onto a gate consumes one condition. At zero the gate stays open until repaired and deliberately closed.
There is one bucket and one hammer. A held tool prevents carrying milk; drop tools for another shepherd to use.
Fill the bucket at the well and pour beside troughs. Repair with the hammer; spare board reloads at the barn are finite.
